Research differentiates between continuous unbroken exposure and cumulative daily volume when assessing autonomic strain, cognitive fatigue, and HPA axis activation:
Continuous Exposure Thresholds (Per Hour)
 * The 45–50 Minute Mark (Cognitive & Autonomic Drop): Studies on sustained visual attention and cognitive load demonstrate that without a break, error rates and sympathetic tone rise sharply after 45 to 50 minutes of continuous screen work.
 * The 50/10 Protocol: Clinical ergonomics and neuroergonomics generally recommend an operating cadence of 50 minutes on / 10 minutes off (or at minimum 5–10 minutes of non-screen recovery every hour) to allow visual accommodation muscles to relax and parasympathetic tone (vagal regulation) to reset.
 * The 20-20-20 Ocular Reset: Every 20 minutes, shift focus to an object at least 20 feet away for 20 seconds. While primarily designed to prevent ciliary muscle spasm and digital eye strain, this visual break also interrupts sustained, narrow foveal focus (which correlates with low-level sympathetic vigilance).
Cumulative Thresholds & Autonomic Impact
 * > 2 Continuous Hours (HPA Axis & Cortisol Shift): Binge-watching or continuous gaming/scrolling for over 2 hours without substantial physical movement suppresses Heart Rate Variability (HRV) and elevates salivary cortisol, signaling a sustained stress response rather than a relaxed state.
 * > 4 Hours/Day (Structural & Mood Correlations): Longitudinal neuro-imaging data (such as the ABCD Study) associate recreational screen time exceeding 4 to 7 hours daily with premature cortex thinning in pediatric populations and higher risks of mood dysregulation in adults.
 * The "First & Last 60 Minutes" Rule: Screen exposure within the first 30–60 minutes of waking spikes early cortisol reactivity and primes hypervigilance for the day. Screen use in the final 60–90 minutes before bed suppresses melatonin and disrupts the autonomic drop necessary for restorative slow-wave sleep.
High-Frequency Scrolling vs. Static Reading
 * High-Paced Media (Rapid Cuts / Short-Form Video): Brainwave studies show rapid shifts from alpha waves (calm focus) to high beta/gamma waves (active processing/stress) within 3 to 5 minutes of high-tempo feed interaction due to the continuous micro-surges of dopamine and unpredictable rewards.
 * Static Text/Long-Form: Preserves deeper attentional stability and produces significantly lower autonomic arousal across equivalent time blocks.
